name: The Ashford Vale
coords: Metres on the X/Z ground plane relative to Ashford at (0, 0); pos = [x, z]. The streamed world is 12 x 12 km (+-6144); the original valley is the +-2000 core, the rest is the new land. Matches WorldGen seed 1066: Kingsreach sits at (560, -420). Danger climbs with distance from Kingsreach: danger_tier 1 near the valley, 3 in the far corners.

places.name: Ashford
places.description: The home village: timber-and-thatch houses around a runestone circle, a mill on the stream, the inn, the smithy and the guard post. Founded by folk who came 'out of the ashes' of an older town.

places.name: Kingsreach
places.description: The royal castle-city of Caldrenn, a morning's ride north-east along the King's Ember Road.

places.name: Emberglass Mere
places.description: A still, deep lake south-west of Ashford. At sunset the water turns the colour of embers. Fishers keep a jetty on the east shore; children are warned off the drop-off in the middle.

places.name: The Ashrun
places.flows: from the northern hills south into Emberglass Mere, out of its south-west shore and away toward the Westfen marshes
places.description: A cold, clear river fed by snowmelt. It turns the Ashford mill by a cut channel and is crossed by the Ashrun Bridge on the Oakvale road.

places.name: Ashrun Bridge
places.description: An old stone bridge where the Oakvale road crosses the Ashrun. Toll-free, but the guard sometimes posts a watch here.

places.name: Duskbriar Wood
places.description: Dense old oak and briar south-east of Ashford, past the edge of the runestone ward. Woodcutters work its northern fringe; wolves and goblins own the rest.

places.name: Tuskridge Hold
places.description: A ring of log longhouses on a hilltop beyond Duskbriar Wood, behind an earthwork and stakes. The exiled Tuskridge clan lives here under an uneasy truce with Ashford.

places.name: Mossfang Warren
places.description: A burrow under the roots at Duskbriar's northern edge: tunnels, snares and a stolen-goods midden. The first real fight most Ashford youths face.

places.name: Shrine of the Sleeping Flame

hidden_trigger.hint: An eight-year-old who climbs to the shrine alone and relights the cold brazier.

places.description: Broken pillars and a cracked brazier on a hilltop west of the Ashrun. Older than Ashford; the carvings show a bird rising from fire. Nobody tends it now.

places.name: Cinderpost Waystation
places.description: A walled halfway post on the King's Ember Road with a stable, a trough, a bunkhouse and a patrol post. Caravans water their oxen here; the notice board carries capital news a day late.

places.name: The King's Ember Road
places.description: The main road from Ashford to the capital, running north-east. Kept safe by patrols and a line of waystones; its surface is packed ash and gravel.

places.name: Whisper Hollow
places.description: A mossy dell on the Ashrun just below the Mere where the wind sounds like voices. Something lives under the old willow.

places.name: The Silverrun
places.flows: from the north-eastern foothills south through the eastern lowlands and out to the southern edge of the map
places.description: A broad silver-grey river of the eastern lowlands, fed by the same snowmelt as the Ashrun. Timber bridges carry the far roads across it; the ferrymen say it never quite freezes.

places.name: Mistwood
places.description: A pale, fog-hung wood on the far western edge of the map. Charcoal burners work its fringe and do not go in after dusk.

places.name: Greywood
places.description: Ash-grey trunks south-west of the Mere, older than Ashford. Grimtusk orcs hunt here, and the wolves have learned to fear them.

places.name: Thornwold
places.description: A thicket of black thorn beyond Ironmarch, east of the Silverrun. Poachers, outlaws and worse.

places.name: Ratfang Warren
places.description: A second goblin burrow far west of Ashford, in the hills beyond the Ashrun. Smaller than Mossfang, but bolder.

places.name: Skullpick Warren
places.description: A goblin mining-warren in the north-eastern woods, grown fat on caravans that strayed from the Ironmarch road. Orc mercenaries sleep in its lower tunnels.

places.name: Grimtusk Hold
places.description: A palisaded war-camp in the deep Greywood, far south-west. Unlike the Tuskridge, the Grimtusk want nothing from Caldrenn but its ashes.

places.name: Deepdark Warren
places.description: The oldest goblin warren on the map, at the far north-western edge, where the rim mountains begin. A troll is said to rule the lowest chamber.

places.name: Silverford
places.description: The guild town on the Silverrun ford (WorldGen's Ironmarch): Masons' and Runecarvers' Guild, Merchants' Hall, Adventurers' branch.

places.name: Greenhollow
places.description: The farming village of the meadows (WorldGen's Oakvale): the Pennick farm and the Great Oak.

places.name: Highwatch Keep
places.description: Stronghold of the Order of the Highwatch and the Ember Lancers, on the ridge above Highcliff.

places.name: Highwatch north gate
places.description: The keep's gate, where the road from Highcliff arrives.

places.name: Highwatch Elder Stone
places.description: The Elder Stone before Highwatch's gate.

places.name: Greyseam Elder Stone
places.description: The Elder Stone above the Greyseam rift seam.

places.name: Elden Elder Stone
places.description: The Elder Stone at the end of the Elden Road.

places.name: The rift seam, lower Greyseam
places.description: Where the rift seam runs under Greyseam Mine.

places.name: Glade Elder Stone
places.description: The fallen Elder Stone of the Stagborn Glade (look landmark stagborn_glade).

places.name: Crownstead Elder Stone
places.description: The Elder Stone on the crown of Crownstead Mill Hill (look landmark crownstead_mill_hill).

places.name: Crownstead
places.description: The Crown's farms: the three-windmill hill and the Steward's Hall.

places.name: The Elden Road
places.description: The old runestone road west from the Shrine of the Sleeping Flame to the Elden Elder Stone.

places.name: The Eastern Gate
places.description: Closed border post to the Church realms (Aurelis, Varska, Serathi).
places.hint: Closed by order of the Aurelis Patriarchate.

places.name: Grimfen Pass
places.description: Snowed shut since the Long Dark; the road to the Frostcrown Holds.
places.hint: Snowed shut since the Long Dark.

places.name: Scar Mouth Arena
places.description: The arena before the Ashen Scar's mouth: the optional finale encounter.

places.name: The Rift Mouth
places.description: The violet mouth in the Scar Mouth Arena (story id rift_mouth).

places.name: The Miller's Stone
places.description: The standing stone by the Old Mill Staff Yard.

places.name: Old Mill Staff Yard
places.description: Maren Coldbrook's staff yard, at Ashford's edge.

places.name: Ashford runestone circle
places.description: The ring of stones at the heart of Ashford.

places.name: Masons' and Runecarvers' Guild hall
places.description: The guild hall (interior: guildhall_interior).

places.name: Silverford market
places.description: The market before the guild hall.

places.name: Pennick farm, Greenhollow
places.description: Gilda Pennick's farm.

places.name: Greenhollow's south fields
places.description: The wheat rows on the south edge, where the Scar reaches first.

places.name: The Greenhollow road
places.description: The frontier road between Ashford and Greenhollow.

places.name: Hollowfang Wood
places.description: A dripping wood far to the south, where the road gives out. Charcoal burners say the trees grow in rings, and the rings are older than the Long Dark.

places.name: Duskfen Wood
places.description: Pines and black water in the far north. The trappers of Frostmere will not go in after the second frost.

places.name: Gnawbone Warren
places.description: A goblin warren in the far eastern woods, built around the ribs of something that was never a cow. Orcs and a troll keep it for the goblins.

places.name: Rotspine Warren
places.description: A sprawling goblin burrow beyond the western settlements. Caravans that took the outer road never mention it, because none of them came back.

places.name: Mudtooth Burrow
places.description: A flooded goblin burrow in the northern pines. The tunnels fill and drain with the thaw, and the goblins fight in the dark and the wet.

places.name: Cinderhollow Warren
places.description: An old charcoal pit grown over by goblins, far in the north-east. Smoke rises from it even in the rain.

places.name: Skullmarch Hold

chief.name: Rhogar Skullsplitter
chief.title: Warchief of the Skullmarch
chief.temperament: proud, hungry for a war worth the name

places.description: A palisaded orc hold at the southern edge of the map. The Skullmarch raid whoever the road brings them, and keep the heads on poles to say so.

places.name: Redtusk Camp

chief.name: Dagha Redtusk
chief.title: Warchief of the Redtusk
chief.temperament: patient, ruthless, loves a bargain she can break

places.description: A war-camp in the far western forest, hidden behind the rim hills. The Redtusk trade pelts at the edge of the map and take what they like past it.
